title: Taking a Moment for Reflection
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case for the deliberate pause as a leadership tool during disagreements and emotionally charged moments. Simple phrases like I want to process what I just heard buy time to formulate a thoughtful response instead of a reactive one, and the pause itself lowers the temperature for both parties. The author notes that these statements aren't requests, leaders claim the right to pause as they see fit, and they're rarely resisted because everyone recognizes the maturity behind them. The piece closes with a caution that pausing too often can read as indecisive, but rarely pausing at all leads to responses people come to regret.
points: Smart leaders pause and gather their thoughts before responding during disagreements or charged moments
Simple phrases like I want to process what I just heard buy time and lower the temperature for both parties
These statements function as claims, not requests, and are rarely resisted
Pausing too often can seem indecisive, but never pausing leads to regretted responses
quotes: This gives them the chance to collect their thoughts and convey the message they want to send, not the one that pops into their head.
The pause also interrupts emotional reactions of both parties and typically lowers the temperature of the discussion just enough to make a difference.
It takes maturity, emotional intelligence, and sound judgment to take such a pause, and everyone involved knows it.
Notice the statements are not a request. Leaders claim the right to pause as they see fit.
Leaders who too often allow themselves to get caught up in the emotion or enthusiasm of the moment without taking a moment for reflection often regret their responses and decisions
